extracted.intended_audience: agency administrators, policymakers, congressional staff, and researchers analyzing administrative adjudication/case-processing efficiency
extracted.subtask_description: Metrics and procedural criteria for measuring and reporting agency examiner workload, case dispositions, backlog, use of shortened procedures, and timing of hearings/decisions across administrative adjudications (fiscal year 1957).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of cases pending (snapshot at period start/end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ha. of cases pending July 1, 1956 / Total cases pending June 30, 1957 (per type of proceeding and agency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as absolute counts by agency and type of proceeding (e.g., Social Security, Interstate Commerce) to measure backlog at the beginning and end of the fiscal year; used as baseline for assessing workload and change over the year.

rubrics_metrics.name: New cases assigned during the year
rubrics_metrics.description: New cases assigned during 1957 (per agency and type of proceeding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts of cases newly assigned to examiners during the fiscal year; compared with dispositions and pending counts to evaluate inflow vs outflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old cases remanded during the year
rubrics_metrics.description: Old cases remanded during 1957 (per agency/type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts of remanded matters returned to examiners; important for understanding recurrence and rework in caseload statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases disposed of by examiners during the year
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases disposed of by examiners during 1957 (aggregated and by type of disposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total dispositions produced by examiners in the year; used with pending/new-assigned data to compute throughput and examiner productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition types (breakdown)
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of dispositions: Ex' mrs decision on the merits; Dismissal on procedural grounds; Voluntary withdrawal; Removal from examiner for Agency Action; Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each disposition type is reported separately, and often segregated by whether it occurred before or after hearing. Use to analyze quality, procedural dismissals vs merits determinations, and cases taken away from examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition timing relative to hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of dispositions 'Before Hearing' and 'After Hearing' (for each disposition type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates whether decisions or dismissals occur without evidentiary hearing or after oral hearing; important for assessing reliance on hearings vs shortened procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'shortened procedures' vs evidentiary hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of cases decided on the merits after oral hearing versus number decided on the merits by shortened procedure (procedures permitting decisions without evidentiary hearings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by agency/type of proceeding to show the extent to which examiners issue merit decisions without full evidentiary hearings; includes counts of 'Other dispositions' as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age distribution of proceedings pending before examiners (end-of-year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Age categories for pending cases as of June 30, 1957 (e.g., pending before examiners: 3 mos. or less; 3 to 6 months; 6 to 12 months; over 1 year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure backlog staleness and timeliness; specific age buckets are reported per agency and proceeding type to identify long‑pending cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age distribution of proceedings disposed by examiners during year
rubrics_metrics.description: Age categories for cases disposed by examiners during the year (e.g., 1 mo. or less; more than 1 mo. up to 3 mo.; more than 3 to 6; more than 6 to 12; more than 12 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports time from assignment to decision; used to measure speed of disposition and compare across proceeding types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time from assignment to examiner to decision (after evidentiary hearing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of time (categorized) from assignment to examiner to the issuance of a decision on the merits when that decision followed an evidentiary hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Buckets mirror other timing tables; used to evaluate how long cases that required hearings take to reach a merits decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time from assignment to examiner to opening of hearing (for cases decided after hearing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of time (categorized) from assignment to examiner to the opening of the evidentiary hearing in proceedings where examiners later issued merits decisions after the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures delay until hearing begins; used alongside decision-timing to identify pre-hearing intervals and scheduling performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time from assignment to examiner to decision (without evidentiary hearing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of time (categorized) from assignment to examiner to decision by examiners issued on the merits where no evidentiary hearing was held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses speed of resolutions handled via written record/shortened procedures; separate table for decisions rendered without hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of cases decided on the merits after oral hearing vs by shortened procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: For each type of proceeding, number of cases decided on the merits after oral hearing and number decided on the merits by shortened procedure (and other dispositions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly contrasts oral-hearing outcomes versus shortened-procedure outcomes to evaluate reliance on each and their relative volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counts of cases with hearings prior to examiner decision and submissions-only cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of cases in which hearing was held prior to examiner's decision; number of cases decided on written submissions only (without oral hearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes full hearings from submission-only adjudications; useful for workload planning (hearing days) and assessing the burden of oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner staffing and availability metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiners employed July 1, 1956 and June 30, 1957; number borrowed from/loaned to other agencies during year; total man‑years available to agency fiscal 1957.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing counts and man‑years provide denominators for productivity measures and hearing-day capacity; includes cross-agency loans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing workload per man-year (average days in hearings and conferences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number days in hearings and conferences per man-year (reported by agency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows average hearing-time burden per examiner-year; used to plan staffing and to compute hearing-day productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity: average number of decisions on merits per man-year
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number decisions on the merits per man-year in all types of proceedings (reported by agency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary productivity metric — decisions per examiner-year across proceeding types, used to compare examiner output across agencies and years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total proceedings assigned for conduct of hearing only
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of proceedings assigned to examiners specifically for conduct of hearings (as distinct from other assignments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates hearing-heavy caseloads and allocation of examiners to hearing duties rather than paper adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of footnote adjustments and exceptions in counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported counts may include special-case adjustments: defaults, consolidations, cases certified to the Solicitor, intermediate decisions waived under rule, hearings reopened, voluntary surrenders, change of venue, and counts certified to other decision makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes explain that totals may include default cases, consolidated matters, cases certified to the Solicitor for decision, waivers under rule 1110(c), and other exceptions — these should be considered when comparing or aggregating figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency/type-specific proceeding labels and statutory citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceeding categories are reported with their statutory references (e.g., 'AMA marketing order contests, 7 U.S.C. 603c(15)(A)', 'Appeals from benefit rights determinations, 42 U.S.C. 405').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification by statute/proceeding type enables cross-agency comparisons and indicates legal context for each metric; necessary for mapping metrics to legal/regulatory domains.
